evals.prompt: Define pattern recognition for agent/codebase work and explain why three instances change the response from one-off fixing to systemic prevention.
expected_elements: Defines pattern recognition as identifying recurring structures across instances
Distinguishes one bug, two coincidences, and three pattern candidates
Requires clustering and shared-root verification before codifying
Connects the pattern to durable prevention rather than repeated symptom fixes
Mentions codification through docs, evals, lint rules, hooks, or architecture changes

evals.prompt: Explain the Observe -> Cluster -> Name -> Codify -> Detect -> Prevent loop and identify the failure mode each stage prevents.
expected_elements: Names all six loop stages
Observe prevents premature pattern claims
Cluster prevents grouping similar symptoms without a shared root
Name creates a searchable, discussable pattern handle
Codify and Detect make the pattern reusable and testable
Prevent aims to make recurrence impossible when proportionate

evals.prompt: Distinguish pattern-recognition from debugging, code-review, diagnosis, naming-conventions, lint-overlay, and taxonomy-design.
expected_elements: debugging owns one specific failing instance
code-review owns PR-scope judgment
diagnosis owns per-incident triage before the class is known
naming-conventions owns defining naming rules
lint-overlay owns lint-rule implementation machinery
taxonomy-design owns classification-system design rather than violation detection

evals.prompt: A teammate saw two similar errors and wants to create a new framework and CI lint rule. Diagnose the misconception and correct the response.
expected_elements: Says two similar observations are not enough to declare a pattern
Names the risk as premature codification or pattern inflation
Requires evidence of a shared root cause
Recommends fixing or observing the current instances without over-abstracting
Explains that detection/prevention should be proportionate to recurrence and cost

evals.prompt: A repo has twelve hardcoded color values outside token files, repeated stale import paths, and duplicated null guards. Design a pattern-recognition audit response.
expected_elements: Runs scans/counts before bulk editing
Samples matches to separate true positives from allowed exceptions
Clusters by shared root cause instead of filing duplicate findings
Names specific pattern classes such as design-token drift, stale pattern, or duplicated guard
Proposes prevention through lint/eval/docs/type constraints rather than only fixing instances
